subject: [PATCH v3 02/11] mm, swap: support zswap and zeroswap as vswap backends

2026-08-06.patch_summary: This patch introduces support for virtual swap (vswap) in the Linux kernel, allowing pages to be compressed by zswap or detected as zero-filled without pre-allocating a physical swap slot. It builds on top of the existing swap-table infrastructure and supports zswap and zero-page backends. The vswap layer decouples PTE swap entries from physical backing, enabling efficient compression and detection of zero-filled pages. The patch also adds a sysctl to enable or disable vswap allocation at runtime and introduces a new build option for defaulting vswap on or off. However, it does not yet support physical disk backing or real writeback, which will be addressed in subsequent patches.

reviews.author: Youngjun Park
reviews.summary: Reviewer Youngjun Park questioned whether the vswap layer is actually enabled at populate time and suggested that only validation is needed to ensure it doesn't come in, specifically for free clusters (dynamic ci) where the cluster is freed immediately.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello Nhat

Does vswap actually come in at populate time?
For free clusters (dynamic ci), 
isn't the cluster freed immediately rather than going through this path?

If it is right, then just validation seems good enough. (assure vswap does not come in)

Thanks
Youngjun

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a mistake in cluster_reclaim_range() and agreed to fix it in the next version.
reviews.raw_body:
Acked. You're right I think. This got me staring at the code along
this direction, and I discovered another code path where I provisioned
for vswap's sake unnecessarily (cluster_reclaim_range()) - will fix
this in the next version.

Thanks for the review, Youngjun!

2026-08-15.patch_summary: This patch adds support for virtual swap (vswap) in the Linux kernel, allowing pages to be compressed by zswap or detected as zero-filled without pre-allocating a physical swap slot. The vswap layer is built on top of the existing swap-table infrastructure and supports zswap and zero-page backends. A new sysctl /proc/sys/vm/vswap_enabled is added to enable or disable vswap allocation at runtime, defaulting off unless configured otherwise. Existing virtual entries will continue to resolve their backend and drain naturally when vswap is turned off.

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kunwu Chan noted that a NULL dereference was reported in the v3 series, specifically due to the 'virtual_table' lifetime management introduced by this patch.

Reviewer Kunwu Chan noted that vswap_free() acquires the per-vswap spinlock while holding the folio lock, creating a potential deadlock with reclaim paths when try_to_unmap() is called.

Reviewer Kunwu Chan noted that using `atomic_long_read()` alone is insufficient to ensure the lifetime of the allocation being accessed, and requested additional synchronization

Reviewer Kunwu Chan noted that the virtual_table introduced in this patch does not have an equivalent lifetime rule as the existing ci->table, which can lead to a NULL dereference when __vtable_get() is called after virtual_table has been torn down. He suggested making virtual_table follow the same lifetime scheme as the existing cluster table or tying its freeing to the lifetime of swap_cluster_info_dynamic.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu,  6 Aug 2026 11:42:45 -0700 Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Nhat,
[...]
syzbot reported a NULL dereference in the v3 series:

  __vtable_get()
    vswap_to_phys()
      swap_entry_backend_has_flag()

Seems like the underlying issue is introduced by this patch's
`virtual_table` lifetime management.

This patch adds:

---

[...]

while the read side does:

---

`atomic_long_read()` only makes the access atomic; it does not protect
the lifetime of the allocation being accessed.

[...]

---

The existing `ci->table` already has an RCU-aware lifetime: readers use
the corresponding RCU access rules, and the storage is not freed until
after the appropriate grace period. `virtual_table` introduced here does
not have an equivalent lifetime rule.

The syzbot crash shows that the current teardown/read-side synchronization
is insufficient: `__vtable_get()` can observe a torn-down
`virtual_table` and dereference NULL.

I don't think a NULL check in `__vtable_get()` alone would be the right
fix. The NULL dereference is a symptom of the missing lifetime guarantee.
`virtual_table` needs to remain valid for as long as a reader can reach
and access the corresponding dynamic cluster.

It probably makes sense to make `virtual_table` follow the same lifetime
scheme as the existing cluster table, or otherwise tie its freeing to the
lifetime of `swap_cluster_info_dynamic`.

[...]


Thanks,
KunWu
